Here are the extracted quantitative parameters and values from the text:

1. CD69 expression by recently activated T cells is transient (98).
2. Activated T cells undergo several rounds of division before downregulating CD69 (8, 22).
3. CCR7 expression levels impact the time T cells spend in lymph nodes (LNs) (22).
4. CCL21 levels are highest toward the LN center and decrease toward the peripheral medullary areas (25, 99).
5. T cells devoid of CCR7 (CCR7\textsuperscript{−/−}) egress more rapidly than wild-type (WT) counterparts (22).
6. T cells in the absence of CCR7 egress more slowly in efferent lymphatics than WT counterparts (22).
7. More CCR7\textsuperscript{−/−} than WT T cells entered sinuses (22).
8. CD4\textsuperscript{+} T cells devoid of LFA-1 had a greater tendency to egress across sinuses and spent less time in the LN than WT counterparts (26).
9. Antibody-mediated blockade of CLEVER-1 or MR reduced binding of lymphocytes to sinus endothelium (81, 82).
10. Antibody-based blockade of α9 or tenascin-C deficiency resulted in impairment of T cell egress from inflamed LNs (83).
11. T cell migration and egress occurs both at the level of the cortical and medullary sinuses (23, 101).
12. T cells were observed entering sinuses at multiple locations, occasionally two or more T cells entered at specific “hot spots” (23).
13. T cells migrated at the same speed through cortical sinuses without flow as through the parenchyma (23, 24).
14. CD4\textsuperscript{+} T cells migrate more efficiently through afferent lymphatic vessels (LVs) than CD8\textsuperscript{+} T cells (43, 44, 62).
15. Adoptive transfer studies, crawl-out experiments, and studies in Kaede mice demonstrate that CD4\textsuperscript{+} T cells more efficiently exit the tissue via afferent LVs (7, 31, 102).
